1.he: למיחסי האיך והמתי אל מאמרות שונים
1.note: Probably refers to those who assign the 'how' (building) and 'when' (years) of the Temple's greatness to different categories (Aristotelian), so 'greater in years' would not fit a 'glory' statement; sense uncertain.

2.he: דתרי הרוב שלישי יעמוד עד נצח
2.note: The phrase דתרי הרוב is obscure (perhaps 'of which two were destroyed'); translated by context.

3.he: ספר י"א פרק י"א מן הקדמוניות
3.note: The tomb episode of Herod is in Josephus, Antiquities 16.7.1; the author's book number is retained as given.

4.note: Literal 'while grazing the asses'; the reference to Numa in Livy is unclear here, possibly a garbled allusion. Translated literally.

5.he: לא יהא אלא כי יחם לבבם
5.note: The argument (that hostile pagan writers would have exposed fabrications, so their testimony to Jewish honor is credible) is compressed; the rendering is tentative.

6.note: Josephus (War 5.5.3) speaks of Alexander, father of Tiberius [Julius Alexander], not of the emperor; the author's identification is kept.

7.note: Josephus says Alexander overlaid nine gates; the details of the women's gate are compressed by the author.

8.note: Apparently a Hebrew rendering of De civitate Dei ('of [the] City of God'); the form is unusual.

9.note: Josephus (Ant. 14.7.1) gives the mina as two and a half litrai; the figure 150 ounces is the author's (or his source's).

10.note: Josephus names the island of Cos (Ant. 14.7.2); 'Kios' is rendered as transliterated.

11.note: Philo's letter speaks of shields set up in Herod's palace in Jerusalem, not in the Temple; the author's wording is kept.

12.he: אחרי המיתו את אשתו ואת בניו
12.note: The sense of this curse-like clause is obscure; rendered literally.

13.note: No son Monobaz of Agrippa II is known; the author's statement is reproduced.

14.note: Josephus names Pollion and Sameas; the author's question mark is retained.

15.note: The Helena famine passage is Ant. 20.2.5; the author's chapter numbers are kept.

16.note: Sense unclear: apparently that Izates is the one the rabbis call Monobaz.

17.note: Literally 'who belonged to Hanin the high priest'; Josephus' Eleazar son of Ananias. Rendered 'whose father'.

18.note: The objection 'it is obvious' (because of the bat kol) is in b. Berakhot 52a; rendered as given.

19.note: The Talmud's wording is compressed; translation follows the sense of b. Yoma 21a.

20.note: The oil-jar miracle in 2 Kgs 4 concerns the prophet's widow, not the Shunammite; the author's wording is kept.

21.note: The quoted verse is Ezra 4:15; the reference as printed (1:4, perhaps meaning chapter 4) is kept.

22.note: Read as 'and even if' (ואף אם/ויהא); sense from context.

23.note: Abbreviation unclear; perhaps the Jerusalem Talmud of Ta'anit chapter 2. Rendered tentatively.

24.he: אחרי הרגישם על קדושתו כי נזורה אחור
24.note: Syntax compressed; the sense seems to be that the raven-scarer was added when they sensed the Temple's sanctity had declined.
